sentences.text: Dryosaurus is a genus of two known species of ornithopod dinosaurs that belong to the Dryosauridae family.
The genus was named by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1894.
Its mouth included a horny beak and cheek teeth adapted for processing vegetation.
The animal had short arms with five fingers on each hand.
The name Dryosaurus comes from Greek words meaning 'tree' and 'lizard', reflecting a presumed forest-dwelling lifestyle rather than the shape of its teeth.
A hatchling found in Utah showed that young Dryosaurus had proportionally large eyes and short muzzles, which changed as they grew.
Rodney D. Scheetz and his family discovered a Dryosaurus fossil site near Uravan, Colorado, in 1972.
Fossils have been found at sites including Bone Cabin Quarry, the Red Fork of the Powder River, and Lily Park.
Dryosaurus primarily ate low-growing vegetation found in ancient floodplain environments.
Dryosaurus was a quick and agile runner that used its stiff tail as a counterbalance while moving.
Researchers suggest that Dryosaurus relied on its speed as its primary defense against carnivorous dinosaurs.
Dryosaurus lived during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages, approximately 154.8 to 143.1 million years ago.
Dryosaurus shared its environment with giant sauropods including Brontosaurus, Camarasaurus, and Apatosaurus.
It is debated or unknown what the true adult size of Dryosaurus was because no adult specimens have been found.
Recent research by Krumenacker et al. (2026) describes three iguanodontian specimens from the Morrison Formation that have a morphology distinct from Dryosaurus and Camptosaurus.
